# SURF — shared brief for every node (read fully before acting)

Repo: /Users/chaser/surf. Host: macOS arm64, cargo 1.97 stable, Google Chrome at `/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome`, Playwright Chromium builds under ~/Library/Caches/ms-playwright, Apostate (a Chromium fork) under ~/Library/Caches/apostate — Apostate is NOT a dependency; Surf must work with stock Chrome. Commit style: small conventional commits (`feat(cdp): …`), no attribution trailers. Never commit secrets. Do not touch ~/apostate.

## What Surf is
A small indentation-based scripting language plus a Rust runtime for driving Chromium over raw CDP with zero boilerplate. The 90% case is one browser, one tab — so the language makes that implicit. Scripts are IO-bound; the runtime is single-threaded async (tokio current_thread + LocalSet), values are `Rc`, thousands of CDP streams on one thread is fine.

## The philosophy (why it exists)
CDP is an IPC protocol — JSON frames over fds or a websocket. Nothing inside a page's V8 sandbox can observe the IPC layer. "CDP detection" catches SIDE-EFFECTS of how frameworks use it: `--enable-automation` (→ navigator.webdriver, infobar), `Runtime.enable` (console-serialisation getters fire + stack traces captured — this is what Cloudflare/DataDome key on), main-world script injection, blanket `DOM.enable`/heavy domains, and headless-mode rendering gaps. Surf refuses to produce those side-effects, not as a "stealth mode" but because a transparent tool has no reason to. There is no `stealth:` flag; quiet is the only mode.

## QUIET RULES (hard; judges grep for violations)
1. NEVER send `Runtime.enable`. Execution contexts come from `Page.createIsolatedWorld{frameId, worldName, grantUniveralAccess:true}` → `executionContextId`; evaluate with `Runtime.callFunctionOn{executionContextId,…}` / `Runtime.evaluate{contextId}`. `Runtime.addBinding{executionContextId}` + `Runtime.bindingCalled` is the isolated-world → runtime channel (fires without Runtime.enable; verify once in a test).
2. NEVER pass `--enable-automation`, `--disable-blink-features=AutomationControlled`, or any `--disable-*` the user did not ask for. Flags Surf passes: `--remote-debugging-pipe`, `--user-data-dir=<dir>` (ALWAYS — Chrome ≥136 silently ignores pipe/port on the default profile), `--no-first-run`, `--no-default-browser-check`, `--window-size=W,H`, `--headless` (only when headless), `--proxy-server=` (browser-level proxy, credentials stripped), user `flags`, then `about:blank`.
3. `Page.enable` (refcounted, for lifecycle/dialog events) is the ONLY domain enabled by default. `Network`/`Fetch` are enabled only while a hook/intercept/proxy-auth needs them and disabled when the last one is removed. NEVER `DOM.enable` — `DOM.getContentQuads`, `DOM.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded`, `Input.*`, `Page.captureScreenshot`, `Storage.*`, `Emulation.*` all work without enabling their domains.
4. Default transport is the pipe: Chrome reads fd 3, writes fd 4; framing is UTF-8 JSON + a single `\0` byte per message (`--remote-debugging-pipe=cbor` exists; not used in v0.1). Windows uses `--remote-debugging-io-pipes=<readHandle>,<writeHandle>`. No listening TCP port unless the user writes `cdp: 9222`.
5. Scripts never inject into the main world. Helper functions (selector resolver, mutation observer) live in the isolated world under random names.

## LANGUAGE (docs/language.md is the authoritative expansion of this)
- Indentation blocks with `:`; spaces only; `#` comments; a leading `#!` shebang line is a comment. No braces, semicolons, `await`, `let`, `const`. Assignment `x = 1`. Strings `"…"` with `{expr}` interpolation. Durations are literals: `500ms 2s 3m 1h`. Lists `[1,2]`, maps `{a: 1, "b": 2}`, ranges `1..50` / `1..=50`. Calls take positional and keyword args: `click("#a", timeout: 5s)`. Operators: + - * / % == != < <= > >= and or not. `if/elif/else`, `for x in xs:`, `while`, `loop`, `break`, `continue`, `fn name(a, b):` + `return`, lambdas `fn(a): a + 1`, `try: … catch e: …`, `print(x)`, `emit x` (JSON line to stdout), `exit` / `exit(1)`, `sleep(2s)`.
- Config block, top of file, declarative (nothing launches until the first action): 
```
browser:
    path: "/usr/bin/chromium"      # optional; auto-discovery otherwise
    cdp: pipe                      # default | 9222 | "ws://…" (attach to running)
    pool: env("BROWSER_POOL_URL")  # remote provider (wss://) — same script, no code change
    proxy: "http://user:pass@host:8080"
    proxies: ["…", "…"]            # rotation list for shift_proxy()
    headless: false                # default: headed if a display exists
    virtual: true                  # Linux: Xvfb managed automatically
    size: "1280x800"
    profile: "./profiles/alice"    # persistent user-data-dir
    flags: ["--lang=en-US"]
    timeout: 30s
    engine: chrome                 # `apostate` reserved for later (clear 'not yet' error)
```
`browser work:` declares a named browser; `work.page(2).goto(…)`.
- Implicit page rules: a page is a tab. `page` = the sole page of the default browser, auto-created on first use. `page(2)`, `page("login")` auto-create (names map to indices in creation order). Bare actions (`goto click type fill press hover check select scroll text html attr value exists count all wait wait_gone wait_text wait_url eval screenshot pdf url title back reload cookies set_cookie …`) and `browser.goto(…)` resolve to the sole page; with several open the error says `several pages are open (1, 2, "login") — say which: page(2).click(…)`.
- Selectors: CSS default; `text=Buy now`; `xpath=//a` or `//a`. Every action auto-waits (attached, visible, stable, enabled) up to `timeout`.
- `eval("document.title")` / `eval(fn(): document.cookie)` runs in the isolated world and returns JSON values.
- Reactive handlers: `on element_appears(".checkout"):` body runs on its own task when the element shows up (isolated-world MutationObserver → binding); also `on navigation(pattern)`, `on dialog`, `on request(pattern)`, `on response(pattern)`, `on message` (inside actors). A program stays alive while handlers are registered or tasks run; `exit` ends it.
- Concurrency: `spawn f(args)`; `parallel for x in xs:` (optional `limit: N`, `fail_fast: true`); each task that uses bare actions gets its own page.
- `task name(params):` with leading property lines `retry: 5`, `on_fail: shift_proxy()`, `timeout: 60s`, `fresh: true`; then statements.
- `actor Name(params):` runs with its own page and mailbox; `send(ref, msg)`, `broadcast(msg)`, `receive()` / `wait_for_message()` (`receive(timeout: 5s)` → nil), `self.id`.
- `supervisor Name:` properties `strategy: one_for_one|one_for_all`, `max_restarts: 3`, `within: 60s`; body is `spawn …` lines and `parallel for … : spawn …`.
- Properties-before-statements rule: inside task/actor/supervisor bodies, leading `ident: expr` lines are properties; after the first statement they are a syntax error.
- The canonical examples: examples/hello.surf (`page.goto("https://example.com")` / `print(text("h1"))`), examples/login.surf (EXACTLY: a `browser:` block with `    virtual: true`, blank line, `page.goto("https://example.com/login")`, `type("#username", "user")`, `type("#password", "pass")`, `click("#submit")`), examples/two-tabs.surf (`page(1).goto(…)`, `page(2).goto(…)`, `page(1).type(…)`), examples/scrape-emit.surf (for over `all("a")`, `emit {text: a.text(), href: a.attr("href")}`), examples/parallel-pool.surf, examples/supervised.surf (Scout broadcasts a token; Workers receive and use it under a supervisor).

## PUBLIC CONTRACTS (skeletons written at scaffold; implementers keep these shapes)
surf-cdp (Send + Sync; tokio::sync internally):
```rust
pub trait Transport: Send { fn send(&mut self, frame: &[u8]) -> BoxFuture<'_, io::Result<()>>; fn recv(&mut self) -> BoxFuture<'_, io::Result<Option<Vec<u8>>>>; }
pub struct Connection; impl Connection { pub fn new(t: Box<dyn Transport>) -> Arc<Connection>; pub fn root(&self) -> Session; pub async fn attach(&self, target_id: &str) -> Result<Session, CdpError>; pub fn set_trace(&self, on: bool); pub fn is_closed(&self) -> bool; }
pub struct Session; impl Session { pub async fn call<P: Serialize, R: DeserializeOwned>(&self, method: &str, params: P) -> Result<R, CdpError>; pub async fn call_raw(&self, method: &str, params: serde_json::Value) -> Result<serde_json::Value, CdpError>; pub async fn send<C: Command>(&self, c: C) -> Result<C::Response, CdpError>; pub fn events(&self, method: &str) -> tokio::sync::broadcast::Receiver<Event>; pub async fn enable_domain(&self, domain: &str) -> Result<DomainGuard, CdpError>; pub fn session_id(&self) -> Option<&str>; pub async fn detach(&self) -> Result<(), CdpError>; }
pub struct Event { pub method: String, pub params: serde_json::Value, pub session_id: Option<String> }
pub enum CdpError { Protocol { code: i64, message: String, method: String }, Closed, BrowserCrashed { exit_code: Option<i32>, stderr_tail: String }, Io(std::io::Error), Json(serde_json::Error), Timeout { method: String } }
```
surf-vm (single-threaded; wasm32-clean; `futures::future::LocalBoxFuture`):
```rust
pub enum Value { Nil, Bool(bool), Int(i64), Float(f64), Str(Rc<str>), List(Rc<RefCell<Vec<Value>>>), Map(Rc<RefCell<IndexMap<Rc<str>, Value>>>), Duration(std::time::Duration), Fn(Rc<Closure>), Native(Rc<dyn NativeObject>) }
pub struct Args { pub positional: Vec<Value>, pub kwargs: IndexMap<Rc<str>, Value> }
pub trait NativeObject { fn type_name(&self) -> &str; fn call_method<'a>(&'a self, vm: &'a mut Vm, name: &str, args: Args) -> LocalBoxFuture<'a, Result<Value, RuntimeError>>; fn get_prop(&self, name: &str) -> Option<Value> { None } fn to_json(&self) -> Option<serde_json::Value> { None } }
pub trait Host { fn declare(&self, decl: Declaration); fn resolve_global(&self, name: &str) -> Option<Value>; fn call_global<'a>(&'a self, vm: &'a mut Vm, name: &str, args: Args) -> LocalBoxFuture<'a, Result<Value, RuntimeError>>; fn spawn<'a>(&'a self, vm: &'a mut Vm, name: &str, args: Args) -> LocalBoxFuture<'a, Result<Value, RuntimeError>>; fn parallel_for<'a>(&'a self, vm: &'a mut Vm, items: Value, body: Rc<Closure>, opts: Args) -> LocalBoxFuture<'a, Result<Value, RuntimeError>>; fn sleep<'a>(&'a self, d: Duration) -> LocalBoxFuture<'a, ()>; fn print(&self, s: &str); fn emit(&self, v: &Value); fn fs<'a>(&'a self, op: FsOp) -> LocalBoxFuture<'a, Result<Value, RuntimeError>>; fn env(&self, name: &str) -> Option<String>; }
pub enum Declaration { Config { name: String, alias: Option<String>, props: IndexMap<Rc<str>, Value> }, Fn { name, closure }, Task { name, params, props, body: Rc<Closure> }, Actor { … }, Supervisor { name, props, body }, Handler { event: String, args: Vec<Value>, body: Rc<Closure> } }
pub struct RuntimeError { pub message: String, pub span: Option<surf_syntax::Span>, pub cdp_method: Option<String>, pub selector: Option<String>, pub cause: Option<Box<dyn std::error::Error>> }
pub struct Vm; impl Vm { pub fn new(host: Rc<dyn Host>, globals: Rc<Globals>) -> Vm; pub async fn run(&mut self, program: &CompiledProgram) -> Result<(), RuntimeError>; pub async fn call(&mut self, f: Rc<Closure>, args: Args) -> Result<Value, RuntimeError>; pub fn cancel_token(&self) -> CancelToken; }
```
surf-browser: `Page` is a stable handle (`Rc<PageInner>`) whose backing `{session, target_id, browser_context_id, frame_id}` can be replaced by `rebind(new_backing, Migration{cookies, storage, url})` with cookie/localStorage migration via `Storage.getCookies/setCookies` and an isolated-world eval. This one mechanism serves supervisor restarts, `shift_proxy()`, and later per-page Apostate personas (one process per persona; a logical `Browser` may own several OS processes). Page lifetime rule: handler blocks keep the program alive; `exit` tears everything down.

## DECISIONS (already made — do not re-litigate; recorded in DECISIONS.md)
1. Bytecode stack VM, no Cranelift JIT: scripts are IO-bound, VM gives <5 ms cold start, and runs on wasm32 later. 2. Hand-written lexer (INDENT/DEDENT) + recursive-descent/Pratt parser with ariadne diagnostics; no nom/chumsky. 3. serde_json first (RawValue passthrough); simd-json only with a profile. 4. No `stealth:` flag; quiet is the only mode. 5. tokio current_thread + LocalSet; VM values Rc; surf-cdp Send for future sharding. 6. Indentation syntax, implicit page rules as above. 7. Apostate is a later optional `engine: apostate` + `persona:`; core never depends on it. 8. `pool:` = remote ws provider in v0.1; wasm/edge build later; surf-syntax/surf-vm must stay wasm32-clean. 9. Reactive DOM via isolated-world MutationObserver + Runtime.addBinding/bindingCalled, never DOM.enable. 10. Page identity decoupled from CDP target (rebind) — see contracts. 11. Codegen typed CDP structs from vendored protocol JSON for an allowlist of domains; everything else goes through `call_raw`.

## Definition of done for every node
`cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` green; tests that need Chrome skip with a printed message when none is found (`SURF_CHROME` env overrides discovery) but MUST run on this Mac; docs updated in the same commit as the behaviour; report what you built, what you measured, and anything you deferred (add it to TASKS.md).

# YOUR TASK: scaffold the repository (step 1 of 11)

Working directory: /Users/chaser/surf (currently empty except .empryo/). Do everything inside it.

Create:
1. `Cargo.toml` workspace with members `crates/*`, `[workspace.dependencies]` pinned to current stable versions (verify each with `cargo search <name> --limit 1`): tokio (features rt, macros, io-util, net, process, sync, time, fs, signal), serde (derive), serde_json (raw_value), tokio-tungstenite (native-tls or rustls), futures, thiserror, tracing, tracing-subscriber, clap (derive), ariadne, tempfile, regex, dirs, indexmap, insta (dev), axum (dev), libc, windows-sys (target windows). Release profile: lto="thin", codegen-units=1, strip=true, panic="abort" is NOT allowed (we need unwinding for try/catch in VM? no — VM errors are values, but keep panic default anyway).
2. `rust-toolchain.toml` → channel "stable".
3. Six crates under `crates/`: surf-syntax, surf-vm, surf-cdp, surf-browser, surf-runtime, surf-cli (bin name `surf`). Each with a `src/lib.rs` (or main.rs) that compiles, a module layout matching docs/architecture.md, and `//!` crate docs stating its responsibility. surf-syntax and surf-vm must have NO dependency on tokio/std::process/std::fs in their default features (they must stay wasm32-clean); surf-vm may depend on `futures` for LocalBoxFuture.
4. `docs/architecture.md`: crate map, data flow (script → surf-syntax → surf-vm → surf-runtime → surf-browser → surf-cdp → transport → Chrome), and the PUBLIC CONTRACTS verbatim from the brief (Transport, Connection, Session, CdpError, Value, NativeObject, Host, Page/backing indirection, handler-block lifetime rule). Write the contract Rust signatures as real `pub trait`/`pub struct` skeletons in the crates (bodies `todo!()` or minimal) so parallel implementers compile against the same shapes.
5. `docs/language.md`: the full grammar and semantics from the brief's LANGUAGE section, expanded into a reference with one example per construct. This is the spec the parser and VM will be built to — be precise about indentation rules, duration literals, string interpolation, keyword args, config blocks, task/actor/supervisor headers with `key: value` property lines, `on <event>(args):` handler blocks, implicit page rules, `spawn`, `parallel for`, `broadcast`/`receive`, `exit`.
6. `DECISIONS.md` with the 11 decisions from the brief and their reasons. `TASKS.md` backlog: apostate engine (`engine: apostate`, `persona:`), per-page fingerprints via process-per-persona + Page rebind, WASM/edge target, CBOR pipe framing, main-world eval (addBinding technique), `schedule:` blocks, `surf fmt`, modules/imports, LSP + VS Code grammar, thread-per-core sharding, frames API.
7. `README.md` (condensed philosophy: CDP is IPC, tells are side-effects, quiet by default; the 4-line login example; install; link to docs), `AGENTS.md` (working agreement: crate map, the quiet-CDP rules as hard rules, how to run tests with a real Chrome — `SURF_CHROME` env or auto-discovery, commit style: small conventional commits, no attribution trailers), `LICENSE` (MIT, copyright heretic-tech 2026), `.gitignore` (target/, .empryo/*.db*, .empryo/sessions/, .empryo/genome-writer.lock*, *.log, /tmp-profiles/).
8. `protocol/browser_protocol.json` + `protocol/js_protocol.json` downloaded from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ChromeDevTools/devtools-protocol/master/json/ with the commit/date recorded in `protocol/VERSION`.
9. `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: fmt --check, clippy --all-targets -D warnings, cargo test on ubuntu-latest (install google-chrome via browser-actions/setup-chrome, xvfb) and macos-latest; an `e2e` job that runs `cargo test --test e2e` with SURF_CHROME set.
10. `examples/` with the 6 example scripts named in the brief written to the spec (they will not run yet — that is fine).
11. `git init`, initial commit. Then if `gh` is installed and authenticated (`gh auth status`), run `gh repo create heretic-tech/surf --private --source=. --push`; if `gh` is unavailable or heretic-tech org is not accessible, create under the user's account instead, and if that also fails, skip the remote and say so in your report.

Acceptance: `cargo build --workspace` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass; `cargo build -p surf-syntax -p surf-vm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` passes if that target is installed (try `rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown`; if it cannot be installed, note it and move on). Report the exact files created and the git remote URL.
